rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.4 and 3 - the authors process 2779 filtered water-withdrawal metering records from the Chilean DGA, join them to the water-rights cadastre, derive monthly METRIC AET from Landsat (2019-2022) for 27 paddocks and a 98.6 km2 area, and train a random forest to predict withdrawals from AET and rainfall (Fig. 10, R2 0.64).
rows.notes: The study does not test or report any result on using remote-sensed ET time series to dynamically adapt water allocation or to make the allocation system more resilient to seasonality or climate change. What it shows is a precondition: remote-sensing AET correlates moderately with reported withdrawals (R2 0.33 regression, 0.64 random forest), that reported withdrawals are ~20-25% of granted rights, and that AET plus distance-to-rights can map auditing priority. Adaptive allocation and resilience are only discussed as potential applications in the Discussion/Conclusions, not demonstrated. Hence Q2 no and upstream.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.4 and 3 - own processing of DGA withdrawal metering records, water-rights cadastre, Landsat-based METRIC AET for 27 sites and a 98.6 km2 AOI, and a random forest model of withdrawals validated by 10-fold cross validation (Fig. 10, Fig. 11).
rows.notes: No water-conservation (water-saving) outcome from remote sensing is measured or modelled. The study reports the relationship between AET and withdrawals, field application efficiencies (median ~80%, Fig. 11a), and an auditing-priority raster (Table 2); it suggests these could support auditing and governance, but any reduction in water use or improved allocation is only proposed, not demonstrated. Q2 no; upstream (provides a monitoring/auditing input rather than the claimed conservation effect).

notes: Full text appears complete (sections 1-5, references). Supplementary figures S1-S7 referenced but not included; they do not change the assessment that the study demonstrates correlation/auditing potential of remote-sensing AET rather than adaptive allocation, resilience or water conservation outcomes.
